# covidmortality

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The `covidmortality` package explores patterns in COVID-19 mortality in Australia between 2020 and 2024. It examines how registered COVID-19 deaths changed over time and how these patterns varied across different states and territories and socioeconomic disadvantage groups.

The package provides cleaned datasets and analytical functions to support the exploration and comparison of COVID-19 mortality patterns across Australia.

## Package overview
The `covidmortality` package includes:

- **Data**: Cleaned datasets on monthly national COVID-19 deaths, annual deaths by state and territory, and annual deaths by socioeconomic status (SEIFA), as well as geographical boundaries for mapping.
- **Analysis functions**: Functions to summarise mortality counts and calculate changes in deaths between selected years.
- **Interactive visualisation**: A Shiny application for exploring temporal, geographical and socioeconomic patterns in COVID-19 mortality.

The goal of `covidmortality` is to make the data accessible and facilitate exploratory analysis of COVID-19 mortality patterns in Australia.

## Installation

You can install the development version of covidmortality from [GitHub](https://github.com/ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-pbzhangg) with:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-pbzhangg")
```

## Launching the Shiny application
After installing the package, launch the interactive application using:
``` {r, eval = FALSE}
covidmortality::run_app()
```

## Data
The package includes four datasets covering COVID-19 mortality in Australia between 2020 and 2024.

### covid_state
COVID-19 deaths by state and territory of registration.

- `state`: Australian state or territory abbreviation.
- `year`: Year of death registration (2020-2024).
- `deaths`: Number of registered deaths due to COVID-19.

Source: Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), [COVID-19 Mortality in Australia: Deaths registered until 31 January 2024.](https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/covid-19-mortality-australia-deaths-registered-until-31-january-2024#deaths-due-to-covid-19-state-of-registration)

### covid_seifa
COVID-19 deaths by quintile of socioeconomic disadvantage, based on the ABS Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA).

- `SEIFA Quintile`: Socioeconomic disadvantage quintile, ranging from 1 (most disadvantaged) to 5 (least disadvantaged).
- `year`: Year of death registration (2020-2024).
- `deaths`: Number of registered deaths due to COVID-19.

Source: Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), [COVID-19 Mortality in Australia: Deaths registered until 31 January 2024.](https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/covid-19-mortality-australia-deaths-registered-until-31-january-2024#deaths-due-to-covid-19-socio-economic-status-seifa-)

### state_geom
Geographical boundaries for Australian states and territories, used to support spatial visualisation of COVID-19 mortality patterns.

- `STE_CODE21`: ABS state and territory code.
- `STE_NAME21`: Full state or territory name.
- `AREASQKM21`: Total area of given state/territory in square kilometres.
- `geometry`: Spatial polygon geometry.

Source: Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), [Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3: Digital Boundary Files.](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/access-and-downloads/digital-boundary-files#downloads-for-gda2020-digital-boundary-files)

### covid_monthly
Monthly counts of deaths due to COVID-19 in Australia, organised by month of death occurrence from January 2020 to January 2024.

- `date`: Date representing the first day of each month.
- `year`: Year of death occurrence.
- `month`: Three-letter abbreviation of the month.
- `deaths`: Number of deaths due to COVID-19.

Source: Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), [COVID-19 Mortality in Australia: Deaths registered until 31 January 2024.](https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/covid-19-mortality-australia-deaths-registered-until-31-january-2024#deaths-due-to-covid-19-year-and-month-of-occurrence)

### Data considerations
The mortality datasets contain death counts rather than population-adjusted mortality rates. Therefore, differences in counts should be interpreted with consideration of population size. In particular, comparisons between SEIFA quintiles do not directly measure individual mortality risk.

The ABS data are provisional and may be subject to revision as additional death registrations are received. The state and SEIFA datasets classify deaths by year of registration, whereas the monthly dataset records deaths by month of occurrence. Consequently, these datasets use different time bases and should not be directly compared without considering this distinction.

## Examples

Load the package to access its datasets and analytical functions:

```{r example, results = FALSE}
library(covidmortality)

# Summarise deaths for selected years by state/territory
summarise_state_deaths(years = 2022:2023)

# Summarise deaths for selected years by SEIFA quintiles
summarise_seifa_deaths(years = 2022:2023)

# Calculate distribution of deaths by state for a given year
calculate_death_share(selected_year = 2022)
```
```{r}
# Compare deaths between 2020 and 2022 for all states and territories
calculate_death_change(year_from = 2020, year_to = 2022) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(absolute_change, n = 3) |>
  dplyr::select(-group_type)
```

## AI-Use Declaration
I used ChatGPT to support aspects of this assignment, including data cleaning (CSV import issues, renaming columns with missing names, and converting numerical data to the appropriate type when a comma was present), dealing with errors (such as resolving map rendering issues and investigating possible causes for commands that took a long time to execute), address warnings and notes from devtools::check() (global variable bindings) and suggestions for CSS styling of the Shiny application. I checked and revised all generated code and text before integrating them into my assignment.
